written.myAnswer: Enthalpy (H) is a state property of a system, commonly described as its heat content at constant pressure. Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the difference between the final and initial enthalpies: ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants).
Breaking a bond requires energy to overcome the attractive forces between the bonded atoms, so energy is absorbed.
Glycogen is the body's stored form of glucose. It serves as an energy reserve and can be broken down to provide glucose when needed.

Conversion of hydrated salt into anhydrous salt: endothermic; conduction of electricity by metals: endothermic; burning of paper: exothermic; dissolving ammonium chloride in water: endothermic; vaporizing liquid nitrogen: endothermic; formation of rain from clouds: exothermic; sublimation of dry ice: endothermic; dissolving sodium carbonate in water: exothermic.

Nitrogen and oxygen do not react appreciably under normal conditions because the reaction has a high activation energy, particularly because of the strong N≡N bond. Lightning supplies enough energy to initiate the reaction. When the lightning stops, the energy supply is removed and the reaction stops.

The methane and oxygen mixture needs activation energy to begin reacting; the match supplies it. Once started, the exothermic combustion releases heat that can initiate reaction in more of the mixture, so it continues until a reactant is used up.

Heat is energy transferred between a system and its surroundings because of a temperature difference. Enthalpy is a state property of a system, defined as H = U + pV; at constant pressure, its change equals the heat transferred.
Bond formation lowers the energy of the atoms as they reach a more stable bonded arrangement. The energy difference is released to the surroundings, making bond formation exothermic.
Lipids are an energy store and a component of cell membranes. They also provide insulation and cushioning or protection for organs.

Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for reactants to reach the transition state and begin reacting. The transition state is the short-lived, highest-energy arrangement along the reaction pathway. Aerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose using oxygen, releasing energy and producing carbon dioxide and water.

Cooking provides energy that helps bring about the chemical changes needed to make some foods edible, softer, or easier to digest. Other foods can be eaten without cooking because they do not require those changes.

Fireworks produce spectacular effects because rapid chemical reactions release energy as heat, light, sound, and colored light. The reactions involve fuels and oxidizing agents; metal salts produce many of the colors.
